title: Concept of Social Capital in Community Structures
text:
Social capital refers to the network of relationships and mutual trust that exists within a community. It is defined by the resources accessible to individuals due to their social connections, going beyond mere physical or economic assets.

High levels of social cohesion, often indicated by strong community ties, tend to correlate with better public health outcomes and more stable local economies. When trust mechanisms are robust, collective action becomes easier, allowing communities to address challenges that individual effort alone cannot solve.

Conversely, the erosion of these bonds, perhaps due to rapid urbanization or digital atomization, can weaken the social safety net, making populations more vulnerable to external stressors.
